clue.text: Name ship after European capitalist

parts.note: to dub someone is to give them a name
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: A vessel is named in honour of a European financier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capitalist' looks like a money man, but here it is a resident of a capital city: Dublin, Ireland's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Ireland's capital city is jokingly a European 'capitalist', an inhabitant of a capital.

clue.text: Desert fault

definitions.meaning: to desert one's side or country, going over to the enemy

explanation.definitionFit: To abandon one's country for another is to go over, and a flaw or failing is a shortcoming.

clue.text: Closest I may come to a turning point

indicators.note: these letters may come to form something new once rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone says this is the nearest they will get to a moment of change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may come to' signals that the letters of CLOSEST I can be reworked into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: At midsummer and midwinter the sun's apparent path halts and turns back, an astronomical turning point.

clue.text: A quiet look by doctor showing confidence

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
lo is an old word meaning look! or behold
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A doctor's calm, quick glance reveals self-assurance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just places the pieces side by side; P, LO and MB are standard crossword abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Poise and self-assurance under pressure is the classic sense of composure the word names.

clue.text: Dressing right for part of the service

parts.note: a sauce is a dressing for food

explanation.surface: A salad dressing is just right for part of a meal's service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' suggests a church service or tennis, but it is a tea or dinner service, a set of crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea service is a set of crockery, and the small dish under a cup is one item of it.

clue.text: Scholar took exam, securing first place

indicators.note: securing means holding something firmly within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: sat means took an exam
the van is the front or leading place, as in vanguard

explanation.surface: A student sat the test and came out top of the class.
explanation.definitionFit: A learned person with deep knowledge of a subject is a scholar.

clue.text: Played piano in capitals of Italy and Denmark

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy, and D is the capital (first) letter of Denmark
p (piano) is the musical marking for soft, standing for piano

explanation.surface: Someone played the piano in the capital cities of Italy and Denmark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capitals' does double duty in the surface: a city for Italy, but a capital letter for Denmark.
explanation.definitionFit: Children who romp play boisterously, so the past tense means played about.

clue.text: Conclude it's a nasty deed, when copper admitted being upset

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so one piece goes inside the other
nasty suggests something messed up, so the word's letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so these letters are read backwards in this down clue

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Someone decides a crime was vile when a policeman confessed to being distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' jumbles the deed's letters; 'being upset' turns the copper symbol backwards; 'admitted' puts it inside. 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: To infer or reason out a result from evidence is to conclude it.

clue.text: Well-directed children

parts.note: the nursery-rhyme pair who went up the hill to fetch a pail of water from a well

explanation.definitionFit: The nursery-rhyme boy and girl were sent up a hill for water, so their errand was aimed at a well.

clue.text: Develop and go round topless

indicators.note: topless means losing the top, so the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: to revolve is to go round

explanation.surface: A suggestion to grow and spin about without a top on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes the first letter R from REVOLVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Species or ideas that gradually grow and change over time are said to develop.

clue.text: Goes without saying?

parts.note: read literally, leaving without telling anyone, as someone fleeing secretly does

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who runs off secretly leaves without a word, here read literally from the idiom.

clue.text: Sharing round in pub

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: an inn is a pub
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Friends buy a round of drinks together in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like a round of drinks, but it is the circle-shaped letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Being party to a secret or scheme means being included in it, sharing it.

clue.text: Return a faulty purchase, but apologise

definitions.meaning: bring a defective item back to the shop
withdraw a remark one regrets saying

explanation.surface: A shopper returns a broken item yet ends up saying sorry.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking goods back to the shop and retracting one's words share the same idiom.

clue.text: It's informal — no fee or difficulty

definitions.meaning: costing nothing and posing no trouble

explanation.surface: A casual event costs nothing and is no trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A relaxed, unceremonious manner is described by the idiom, which literally means costless and simple.

clue.text: Troops stepped out in these formations

definitions.text: Troops stepped out in these formations

parts.words: Troops stepped out in these formations
parts.note: military arrangements where each unit is staggered to one side of the one ahead, like steps

explanation.definitionFit: Military formations in which units are positioned in staggered steps carry this name.

clue.text: Nurses go off as doctors appear

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Nursing staff leave their shift just as the doctors arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' signals the rearrangement of NURSES GO; 'as' and 'appear' join it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical practitioners who operate are specialist doctors.

clue.text: Flexitime in violin or tuba playing

indicators.note: playing means performing with, loosely moving the letters about

explanation.surface: A musician takes liberties with tempo when playing violin or tuba.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges OR TUBA. 'Flexitime' looks like working hours but means flexible time in music.
explanation.definitionFit: Musicians speed up and slow down freely for expression, a flexible treatment of tempo.

clue.text: Elevates one among many

indicators.note: among places one piece inside the other

parts.note: hosts means great numbers, many
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone raises one person above the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifting something up with ropes or a crane raises it, so the verb means elevates.

clue.text: Exactly what is needed in employment

definitions.meaning: the perfect thing for the purpose
read literally as merely being at work, just at the work

explanation.surface: Having a job is exactly what someone needs.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means the ideal thing, and literally suggests simply being at work.

clue.text: Idiosyncrasies of surreal artist

indicators.note: surreal means distorted and dreamlike, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The peculiar habits of a surrealist painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Distinctive personal characteristics or quirks are peculiar features of character.

clue.text: Alcohol makes bishop lustful

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
randy is British slang for lustful

explanation.surface: Drink makes a clergyman amorous.
explanation.walkthrough: RANDY is everyday British slang for sexually eager.
explanation.definitionFit: A spirit distilled from wine is a strong alcoholic drink.

clue.text: When corruption is about, I show no respect for authority

indicators.note: is about means surrounds, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: rot means decay or corruption

explanation.surface: Where corruption is rife, a speaker declares disrespect for those in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowd that runs amok and defies the police shows open disorder against those in power.

clue.text: Corresponding but never meeting

definitions.meaning: describing lines that run side by side and never cross

explanation.surface: Matching lives that never actually meet.
explanation.definitionFit: Matching situations are analogous, and lines always equidistant never intersect.

clue.text: A kid feeling relaxed

parts.note: to kid someone is to tease them

explanation.surface: A young goat is feeling comfortable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' looks like a young goat or child, but here it is the verb meaning to rib.
explanation.definitionFit: Being comfortable and free of tension is the idiom's sense, as also in the military command.

clue.text: So reverse and incline to port

indicators.note: reverse means turn back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to tend is to incline towards something

explanation.surface: A sailor is told to back up and head over towards a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverse' turns SO into OS. 'port' looks like the left side of a ship but is a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: The Belgian coastal town is a ferry harbour on the North Sea.

clue.text: The handsome youth said no, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things going wrong, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A good-looking young man regrettably turned someone down.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Aphrodite loved a beautiful young man, whose name now means any handsome youth.
